overview: Sigma 4.11's Phase is an eight-mode clipping module (Spider, Skip, Normal, FullBlock, Silent, HCF, Debug, NCP) that moves the player through solid geometry using three levers: cancelled collision bounds, direct position writes, and crafted C04 position-packet bursts. EventBlockBounds cancels block collision boxes so the player's AABB can overlap blocks (HCF only while inside a block and sneaking, Debug always, all other modes whenever a box's maxY exceeds the player's feet); onEnable arms noClip with zeroed motion when horizontally collided; and the post-phase of EventUpdate pushes the player through walls by rewriting the position with setPosition while sending C04 sequences that teleport the server-side position. The FullBlock, Silent, Normal and Skip modes send bursts of C04 packets - FullBlock pairs the forward move with ten C04s at Double.MAX_VALUE * i and a 9000-block drop, Silent with nine C04s at 8.988465674311579E307, Skip with thirteen alternating low/high C04s from a hard-coded offset array - so the server accepts the wall breach while the client snaps through it. The NCP mode is a noClip walk with teleport nudges (0.617 while speed-boosted, 0.031 otherwise) inside a block, plus a sneak-based descent; the Spider mode rises 0.1 per tick with motionY 0.065 inside a block; the HCF mode drags the bounding box itself. An S08 teleport handler preserves the player's yaw and pitch.

sections.p: onEvent registers EventBlockBounds, EventUpdate, EventPushBlock and EventPacket. EventPushBlock is cancelled outright so pistons cannot shove the player. The EventPacket handler watches outgoing C03 packets: while isInsideBlock() it returns without touching them, and otherwise, when the player is horizontally collided, it mutates every fifth C03 in place (delay counter) by adding the 0.2-scaled input vector to x and z and subtracting 1 from y - the cheapest of the phase paths, since it rides the normal movement stream. The same handler rewrites any incoming S08 yaw and pitch to the player's current rotation and sets shouldSpeed. EventUpdate pre runs the NCP mode's state machine (lastReportedPosY = 0, lastReportedPitch = 999, noClip, motion zeroing, jump handling, pitch jitter, sneak descent, in-block teleports) and EventUpdate post runs the burst modes. onEnable seeds shouldSpeed from isInsideBlock() and starts a 0.006-block teleport when horizontally collided; onDisable restores timerSpeed.

sections.h: Collision cancellation and the NCP walk
sections.p: The EventBlockBounds branch is what makes the client geometry passable: for every mode except HCF and Debug it cancels any block box whose maxY is above the player's feet, so the player's AABB can slide into a block from below; HCF requires the player to be sneaking and inside a block; Debug cancels everything. The NCP mode combines this with per-tick state: while shouldSpeed or inside a block it sets noClip true, zeroes motion and jumpMovementFactor, writes lastReportedPosY = 0 and lastReportedPitch = 999 (so the server's moved-too-quickly comparison and rotation checks see nothing), and presses jump when on an integral y. Inside a block it teleports 0.617 blocks forward (speed variant, with sinusoidal yaw/pitch jitter) or 0.031 otherwise. Sneaking triggers a descent: a full block down when grounded and outside a block (em.setY(Y-1) plus setPosition and motionY 0), or 0.3 blocks every 100ms while inside.

The four burst modes fire from EventUpdate post when the player is horizontally collided and not on a ladder. Normal sends a forward C04 then a second C04 dropping y by 0.09 (9000 over liquid); FullBlock sends the forward C04, ten C04s at Double.MAX_VALUE * i (i = 1..10) and a final drop of 9000 (liquid) or 0.1, with a 0.4 multiplier on the forward vector; Silent sends the forward C04 and nine C04s at 8.988465674311579E307; Skip zeroes half the motion and fires thirteen pairs - a low C04 at posY + OPOP[j] from a 13-entry array (-0.025, -0.0285714, ..., -0.025) and a high C04 at boundingBox.minY with x/z advanced by j times the input vector - then a final onGround-true C04 at the original position. The giant-y C04s exploit vanilla's per-axis limits (x and z are bounded at 3.0E7, y is not), so the server accepts the teleport of the player's server-side position into the wall while the client-side position is snapped with setPosition - the phase is the difference between the two.

files.label: Phase.java (module)
files.explanation: All eight modes share this one file. The EventBlockBounds branch implements the passable-geometry lever with the per-mode conditions; EventPushBlock cancels piston push; the EventPacket handler carries the every-fifth-C03 in-place mutation and the S08 yaw/pitch rewrite; EventUpdate pre runs the NCP mode state machine (including the sneak descent and the 0.617/0.031 in-block teleports through the teleport() helper) and EventUpdate post dispatches the burst modes with their exact C04 sequences. isInsideBlock() scans every block whose collision box intersects the player's AABB (with the BlockHopper full-cube special case) and is the gate that keeps the packet mutations from firing while the player is legitimately inside geometry. onEnable's collided check starts the walk with a 0.006-block teleport.

files.label: PlayerUtil.java (liquid and movement tests)
files.explanation: PlayerUtil supplies the two state tests the burst modes read. isOnLiquid() contracts the player's bounding box by 0.01 on x/z, drops it 0.01, and scans the block at its base for a BlockLiquid - the check that decides whether the burst modes' downward C04 drops 9000 blocks (over liquid) or the small 0.09/0.1 value (on solid ground), because the giant drop is only safe where the server treats the position as fluid-tolerant. isMoving2() reports whether any movement key is pressed and gates the NCP mode's sneak descent, which only fires when the player is otherwise stationary. The same class backs the NoSlowdown module's Hypixel position spoof, which is why the phase module and the noslow module share it.

countering.label: Passable (block ray-trace)
countering.explanation:
NCP's Passable ray-traces the line between the player's previous and current location through the block cache. It uses a PassableAxisTracing with up to 60 steps, first in the vanilla YXZ axis order and then again in alternate orders (YZX or XZY depending on which axis collided), so a phase that hides behind the order of axis resolution is retested. The block-change tracker exempts blocks the server just changed, and on a hit the check returns a set-back location and decays passableVL by 0.99 on clean moves.

The client-side cancellation of EventBlockBounds does nothing server-side: the server still resolves the player's AABB against its own world, and every burst mode's C04 stream moves the server position straight through solid blocks. The one-block drop in the every-fifth-C03 mutation and the 0.09/0.1/9000 drops in the burst modes all cross block boundaries, and the giant-y packets travel from ground into a wall, so the ray trace collides regardless of axis order. The Skip mode's alternating low/high C04 pairs are the closest thing to an evasion (the trace steps between each pair), but each pair still moves through the wall, and the final onGround C04 at the original position re-crosses it. The vertical ray-trace path is the first to trip because the module's drops are pure y-motion with no diagonal component.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement physics envelope)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly's vertical envelope is the second NCP layer the burst modes run into. vDistRel derives the allowed vertical distance from the previous move's momentum and accepts only a zero-y ground move, a jump, a step-up or a riptide launch; everything else is a violation, and the packet's onGround flag is ignored because ground is ray-traced. The module's downward C04s (-0.09, -0.1, -1, -9000, and the OPOP array's -0.2 to -0.025 steps) are none of the accepted envelopes, so each one produces a yDistanceAboveLimit that scales the violation by 100 and triggers the set-back. The ten Double.MAX_VALUE * i C04s of FullBlock produce a y-distance so far beyond the envelope that the violation is effectively immediate and the set-back fires on the first packet of the burst - the client's position snap on the next tick does not undo the server-side violation.

The one legitimate window is the mode's own gate: the mutation branch only fires while isCollidedHorizontally, and the burst modes only fire while collided and not on a ladder - on servers with SurvivalFly enabled those windows are exactly where the set-back will land the player, since the server's physics say the collided state cannot persist through the wall.

countering.label: Phase (tesseract AABB sweep)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's Phase check tests the swept volume between two moves. It inscribes the player's previous and current bounding boxes inside a new AABB and lets planes cut through it along the inscribed boxes, forming a tesseract volume that is then tested against nearby blocks' collision boxes for intersection. The checked volume is shrunk (TOP_EPSILON 0.1, BOTTOM_EPSILON 0.4, SIDE_EPSILON 0.1) to cut false positives, and moves over 65 blocks squared are skipped entirely.

The burst modes fail the sweep in both directions: the forward C04 moves the server position horizontally into the wall (the sweep crosses the block face), and the downward C04s move it vertically through the floor below. The Skip mode's alternating pairs are swept pair-by-pair, and each pair crosses a block boundary. The SIDE_EPSILON shrink is the bypass surface - a phase that keeps the swept volume out of the block's collision box by staying within the epsilon margin passes, which is why the module's 0.006 and 0.031 NCP-mode nudges are near the threshold; the burst modes' full-block steps are not. The 65-block skip does not apply because the module's per-packet moves are small; it is the cumulative wall crossing that trips the sweep.

countering.label: Phase (predicted collision-box intersection)
countering.explanation:
Grim's Phase check runs after every prediction: it takes the player's new bounding box, collects the collision boxes that intersect it, and flags with a set-back whenever the new box intersects a box the old box did not - i.e. the player moved into solid geometry. It skips teleports and ghost-block setbacks, and for 1.8 clients it whitelists anvils, chests and trapped chests because of their glitchy collision in that version. The setback is 1, with a decay of 0.005 per clean tick.

The module's bursts are a direct hit because Grim predicts the move from the player's own physics first: the giant-y C04s (Double.MAX_VALUE, 8.988465674311579E307) cannot be produced by any physics simulation, so the prediction engine rejects them before the Phase check even runs, and the position they land on intersects wall boxes the previous box did not. The every-fifth-C03 mutation (x/z shifted by the input vector, y - 1) is equally unexplained, and the 1.8 block whitelist does not apply to the stone, dirt and cobblestone walls phase is used against. The client-side noClip state is irrelevant - Grim simulates the server world, where the block collision boxes exist regardless of what the client cancelled.
